title: What can you say about vitamin A in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 4 wordings for vitamin A; the strongest is "Supports normal vision" (strong, 120-3,000 µg RAE a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Clears acne, or works like isotretinoin (Accutane)".

supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 19 and older. Health Canada: 65 µg RAE up to about 3,000 µg RAE a day (the maximum differs slightly by source ingredient). EU: at least 120 µg, 15% of the 800 µg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). ODS upper limit for preformed vitamin A: 3,000 µg RAE.
supported_wordings.form: Preformed vitamin A (retinol or its esters), counted in µg RAE

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Clears acne, or works like isotretinoin (Accutane)
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a drug, and acne is a disease.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats macular degeneration or other eye disease

wordings_to_avoid.why: Implies treating infections, which are diseases.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition
